title: sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter ordering and token/event framing in streaming responses
author: Jordan Kim
description:
Context: Several customers and internal fuzz tests flagged cases where SSE streaming responses (OpenAI-compat layer + internal sse_streamer) produced partially-formed JSON events when the model output contained nested JSON fragments and delimiter tokens were split across internal chunks. The bug manifested as invalid partial JSON delivered to clients or events emitted out of token/event order when the continuous-batching runtime flushed KV-cache boundaries. This caused downstream libraries that reassemble streaming JSON to fail (notably when using function/tool-calling or structured output).

This PR addresses root causes across three areas: tokenizer chunk boundary handling, SSE framing/delimiter emission, and the OpenAI compatibility shim's event ordering guarantees. Changes are backward-compatible from the API surface: clients still receive the same SSE event types, but with stronger ordering and safer partial-JSON framing.

Summary of changes: 1) canonicalize delimiter tokens: ensure the streamer treats delimiter tokens ("\n\n", partial-object delimiters) as atomic markers for JSON boundaries and never split them across frames; 2) token->event staging: introduce a lightweight staging buffer that ensures token-level events that belong to the same logical payload are emitted in order even if underlying batch flushes interleave kernels; 3) parser hardening: make the partial-JSON reassembly tolerant of edge cases (truncated escape sequences, split unicode codepoints) and add strict guards to avoid emitting invalid json events; 4) compat layer fixes: reorder finalization hooks so that tool/function-calling finish events and structured-output markers are emitted after the JSON payload is closed; 5) tests: add unit + integration tests that reproduce previous flakiness and new e2e tests exercising OpenAI-compat streaming clients.

Motivation: This is a stability/regression fix affecting streaming-heavy endpoints (chat/complete with streaming, tool-calls, structured-output). Customers using streaming parsers (JS/TS clients, server-side aggregators) saw intermittent JSON.parse errors or missing finalization events which impacted function-calling workflows.

What I changed (high-level): - runtime/streaming/sse_streamer.rs: introduce DelimiterAtom abstraction, adjust flush boundaries and ensure FrameWriter quiesces before emitting delimiter events. - runtime/streaming/parser.rs: add tolerant reassembly for split tokens and codepoint-safe concatenation. - redwood-openai-compat/compat_layer.py: reorder finalize sequence to emit "tool_call"/"function_finish" events after payload close and add an explicit "end_partial_json" sentinel for clients that rely on strict delimiting. - tests/streaming/test_partial_json_delimiters.py: new unit and integration tests (deterministic fuzz cases). - docs/api/streaming.md: note behavior changes and recommended client handling for partial JSON.

CI/QA notes: initial push failed a deterministic integration that simulates split UTF-8 sequences (ci/integration-streaming failed). I updated the parser reassembly logic and added coverage tests; the full pipeline now passes.

Related: ENG-4821 (streaming stability), ENG-4910 (OpenAI-compat function-calling ordering).

review_comments:
Maya Thompson: Can you add a short benchmark to confirm we didn't regress 95th pct latency under small (1-4) batch sizes?
Author (Jordan Kim): Added a microbenchmark in sse_streamer.rs and ran locally; no measurable regression under our load tests. Results summary added to the PR comment.

Ethan Liu: The compat_layer reordering looks correct, but is the end_partial_json sentinel guaranteed to be emitted in case of early cancel/timeout?
Author (Jordan Kim): Yes - the streamer now tracks client-cancel signals and performs a best-effort flush that still emits the sentinel; documented in the streaming.md. There is a small window where upstream abort prevents the sentinel, but the client will receive a truncated close event. We added tests for cancellation behavior.
Priya Nair (approval): Verified the integration test reproduces the previous failure locally and now passes. Approving after CI green.
ci_checks: ci/integration-streaming: pass (initially failed, rerun after parser fix)
release_notes: Fix streaming SSE framing where partial-JSON delimiters or split tokens could produce invalid JSON or reorder events. Improves stability for streaming function/tool-calling and structured output. No API break; recommend clients to handle the explicit end_partial_json sentinel if relying on strict delimiting.
